title: A release leg sets its own TMPDIR on the leg host
body:
hv's ruling of 2026-11-11 (option 1 of kovacs-sysadm's three, devbin-vc's recommendation): a release leg sets its own TMPDIR.

On a Linux leg host, `/tmp` can be a small tmpfs. On kovacs it is systemd's tmp.mount at 50% of 3.3G RAM, 1.7G with usrquota, and an Intent release leg with a large Rust target filled it on the 3.3.0 cut. The stopgap was a hand-added `export TMPDIR="$HOME/tmp"` in kovacs's molt-generated `~/.config/molt/env.sh`, which Molt cannot render: its env liberator publishes a fixed set of variables and refuses values containing `$`.

Ask: the leg's far side (the `ssh host 'bash -s'` run in `lib/release.legs`) exports TMPDIR to a directory inside the leg's own per-run work area on the host's disk, makes it before the gates run, and clears it with the leg's worktree. Uniform for every project's leg, no per-project switch. Once it ships, kovacs's env.sh goes back to its render (kovacs-sysadm removes the hand line). Batched with 0333, the same leg code.

## Resolution

Fixed in two units on main, released in devbin 0.1.23. 0334-1 at 250aadebd44232477ca289075bb52a72a26c1a06, from the tested tip 7d6d3c49, landed after 0333-1, proved on its own arm under hv's rule of 2026-11-05 in one slot on devbin-vc's desk with 0333-1. 0334-2 at 6a261a38743b06c2f5a9219e83b0e950519f37b1 (2026-11-12 11:56Z) landed after the third cut of 0.1.23 stopped red in its kovacs leg, proved in k340's run, at the tested tip 0eae6ab6 with 0341-1, 0340-1 and 0340-2, on 2026-11-12 between 11:09Z and 11:49Z: its arm read red at the base with TMPDIR beside the checkout as a leg's gates are given it, on its own finding, green at the tip with that TMPDIR under BSD and GNU, and ok in both whole suites at the tip, here and in the kovacs leg, the leg that read it red in the cut.

- A remote leg's gates run with their own TMPDIR, <worktree>.tmp on the host's disk beside the run's worktree, exported unconditionally, so it replaces any TMPDIR the host's own startup sets, a shell startup file's default included.
- It is made afresh as the last step before the gates start, so a start refused before it leaves none; what an earlier run at R left there is removed first, made writable, since a build, or a bats run killed mid-file, can leave read-only directories in it.
- It is named in the leg's log, and removed with the worktree when the run is cleared, read-only directories included.
- docs/configuration.md and the release page say so (written with 0335-2).
- 0334-2: harness.bats's arm that holds the suite's temp dir outside the checkout read a temp dir under <worktree>.tmp, the TMPDIR 0334-1 gives a leg's gates, as inside the checkout <worktree>, since it matched a bare prefix of the checkout's name. It now reads a temp dir as inside only when it is the checkout itself or a path under it. A sweep of the tree for the same class, a path matched by a bare prefix of another's name, found no other.

One new arm in releaselegs.bats, red at the base on its own finding (the gates were given the TMPDIR the host's startup set, not the run's own) and green at the fix; it presets a TMPDIR for the start, as a host's startup does, so it shows the export overriding one. 0334-2 added no arm: its proof is that harness arm under a TMPDIR shaped as a leg's, red at the base on its own finding and green at the fix, and green under an ordinary TMPDIR at both. Intent's issue 0682 is met by it, and kovacs's hand-added TMPDIR line in its env.sh can go once a leg passes without it on 0.1.23.
